content.comment_body: What does the ES3 option mean in the hardware selection under the tools menu?

Hello, From what I understand, there is a new hardware revision available (E-Stand 3). Programming this version requires the newest service pack of [product_name] and you need to choose this option when performing a program download. Hope this clarifies things.

Alright [user_name], but what sets the new E-Stand 3 apart from the standard version? There doesn't seem to be any noticeable difference between E-Stand 3 and the standard hardware in the selection menu. Thank you for any information.

Hi [user_name]. The ES3 hardware revision was released with Japanese language support, which wasn't available in the earlier standard version. This was the final language added to the list intended for support. Since it only concerns language, there aren't any changes in the device's functionality or the selection interface. I actually had to contact support for this clarification!

analysis.insight_summary: Users are unsure about the purpose of the 'ES3' hardware option within [product_name] software, as there is little accessible documentation explaining its difference from the standard hardware version. The introduction of Japanese language support in ES3 isn't reflected in functionality changes, which adds to confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for clearer guidance regarding hardware revisions in the software—particularly what sets different versions apart. They want to know the practical impact of selecting ES3 and how it influences programming or device features.
